props.title: The Convergence Queue Is Burned Down
props.subtitle: All 16 lanes of core-runtime-convergence-master-v2 are closed or moved — pushed to main through 2276f521f

props.content: Six milestones, sixteen lanes, one operating rule: a worker's prose is a claim, not evidence. Every verifier was replayed by the controller before anything was called done. This page is the full accounting — what closed, what it left behind, and how it was proven.

props.label: suite results replayed green in the controller shell
MILESTONES
props.title: Six checkpoints from first lint gate to queue complete
props.subtitle: Lanes ran strictly sequentially with a Lore commit between each; read-only audits overlapped where the roadmap marked them parallel-safe

items.title: Boundary lint fails closed + graph cleanup lands
items.description: L11 regenerated the dependency-cruiser gate from canon and proved it with seeded violations. L9 deleted all 28 verified-dead symbols; L10 gave 12 unconsumed exports explicit verdicts (8 deleted, 1 kept with a found consumer). L16's read-only plugins audit ran alongside.

items.title: Eval cutover + one-brain verified with real execution
items.description: L3 cut core/eval over and ran the full dogfood suite through real lev exec — 12 scenarios executed, 4 genuine runtime failures caught that unit tests had missed. L4 replayed all five one-brain verifiers: core/eval is the only truth-decider, zero effect deps across 377 manifests.

items.title: Decompositions, event taxonomy, autodev persistence
items.description: L12 decomposed the four cognitive hotspots behind a real complexity ratchet (graphEpic 185 → 39). L17 renamed run.sealed → execution.sealed at all 8 production sites; L19 deleted core/poly/src/events; L20 closed autodev event convergence.

items.title: Identity vocabulary hard cutover
items.description: L18 renamed run_id → execution_id and exec_id → invocation_id across 147 core files (402 renames), pruned the classification ledger to 14 ruled survivors, retired the residue classifier, and armed full rejection. Root cause of every stale-dist bite found: tsconfig.base paths shadow source with dist.

items.title: Utils lift finished for real, hygiene cleared — queue complete
items.description: L13 deduped output bounding and re-baselined the graph (−2,963 edges). L15 completed slice-0: asRecord single-sourced, core/utils a zero-dependency leaf, every gate controller-replayed. L7 cleared branches, stashes, stale dists, and one dead daemon test. L16 was already done.

props.label: FINAL STRETCH
props.title: What the last two lanes actually fixed
props.subtitle: L15 and L7 looked like bookkeeping. The verification pass turned up two real pre-existing breaks and closed them in passing.

props.content:
The slice-0 completion worker refused to flip its own packet because its sandbox showed red suites — an honest stop. Controller replay proved every one of those reds was environmental: the codex sandbox blocks IPC pipes, localhost binds, and tmux sockets, and the stale-dist mechanism had starved orchestration of a working @lev-os/eval module. With dists rebuilt, the battery came back green.

Two failures survived replay and were real — neither caused by the lift. The task-readiness test fixtures still declared `exec_id` while the validator had been renamed to require `execution_id` (L18 residue; fixing five fixture files also fixed a third failing site in plugins/sdlc, closing bd issue lev-a1p5). And the daemon-pentagon MCP ratchet demanded 21 scenarios when only 16 exist — commit ee96f4f51 had deliberately rewritten five community examples as deterministic non-MCP runnables, so the ratchet was re-anchored to the honest floor of 16.
A worker's prose is a claim, not evidence. Replay the declared verifier yourself before reporting any result as done.

props.label: SPLIT-BRAIN STATUS
props.title: Verified invariants vs. tracked residue
props.subtitle: No undocumented split-brain found across core modules. Every remaining fork of truth has a named owner.

props.title: ✅ Verified by replay
props.content:
**One brain** — core/eval is the only truth-decider; core/effect decides nothing; zero effect deps across 377 manifests (L4, all 5 verifiers replayed).

**One vocabulary** — identity rename executed, classifier retired, rejection armed, 14-entry ruled survivor ledger (L18).

**One event taxonomy** — run.sealed → execution.sealed at all 8 production sites (L17); quad-brain event residue deleted (L19).

**Boundaries fail closed** — seeded eval and telemetry probes both rejected by the regenerated lint gate (L11).

props.title: ⚠️ Known residue, tracked
props.content:
**lev-8fz9** — tsconfig.base paths let stale dists shadow source. Dists were rebuilt, but the mechanism is still live.

**lev-a1z8** — ~60 camelCase `executionId` sites semantically mean per-call invocation, colliding with canon; plus an ~830-hit legacy sweep.

**InvokeEnvelope** — poly-compiler import ruled adopt-or-delete under F1; deletion not yet executed (operator-blocked).

**MCP SDK location** — relocates poly → transport-mcp pending the client-handshake spike (F1, operator-blocked).

props.label: REAL EXECUTION
props.title: Unit tests were not the bar
props.subtitle: The L3 close ran the dogfood suite through real lev exec — and it caught what the unit suites could not

props.content:
Twelve scenarios executed for real. Four failed — every failure a genuine runtime truth invisible to unit tests: a vitest config-resolution bug in our own conversion (fixed, 28 tests green on rerun), the exec package's exports promising a dist layout tsc doesn't emit (lev-suhc), a missing provider card failing the execution-binding preflight (lev-odm8), and a pentagon asserting a file deleted in the harness removal (lev-jhfs). Both lev exec binding probes — codex and opencode adapters — were spot-executed end-to-end and passed.

After remediation the rerun scored 12 executed / 3 failed, with all three remaining reds pre-existing and owned by P1 issues. The standing rule going forward: any *new* dogfood failure is a regression.

props.title: One gate left unproven
props.content: The goal named pi/glm 5.2 as a real-exec target. The evidence trail shows codex and opencode bindings executed for real — but no glm 5.2 profile run. Closing that is a single explicit probe.

props.label: METHODOLOGY
props.title: How every claim was tested
props.subtitle: Six techniques, each forced by a failure mode the session actually hit

props.title: 🔁 Controller replay
props.content: Every worker-declared verifier re-run in the controller shell. Necessary: the codex sandbox produced false reds three separate ways — blocked network, blocked spawns, blocked IPC/tmux sockets.

props.title: 🧪 Stash-roundtrip attribution
props.content: Re-run the failing test at HEAD with the working-tree changes stashed out. This is how the task-readiness reds were proven pre-existing L18 residue rather than a slice-0 regression.

props.title: 🎯 Isolated flake re-runs
props.content: The exec load-flake trio failed 2, then 1, then 3 across full-suite runs — and passed 45/45 isolated. Flakes get named, documented, and re-proven, never waved off.

props.title: 📦 Emit counts, not greps
props.content: tsc exits 0 but emits nothing when dist is deleted and *.tsbuildinfo survives — and a grep over an empty dist is vacuously green. Rebuilds are verified by counting emitted files.

props.title: 🚫 Seeded fail-closed probes
props.content: The regenerated boundary lint gate was proven by planting deliberate violations (eval and telemetry imports) and watching both rule layers reject them — then cleaning the probes.

props.title: 🐕 Real-exec dogfood
props.content: The eval suite executed through real lev exec with live adapter bindings. It found four runtime failures the unit suites could not see. Unit tests are contractor-grade; this is the bar.

Tree clean, main pushed through `2276f521f`, bd sweep recorded, handoff finalized at `.lev/pm/handoffs/20260702-roadmap-burn-down-session-6.md`. The follow-ups table above is the entire live surface: seven bd lanes ready for tasking, three workstreams awaiting operator review.
